page.title: VPN
page.description: Connect through your own servers and choose where your traffic comes out.

install.title: Install the VPN
install.body: Installing downloads nothing. The control server starts on this machine when you turn it on, at an address in one of your domains.
install.askAdmin: The VPN is not installed. An administrator can install it from Apps.

errors.notRunning: The VPN is off. An administrator can turn it on in the Overview.
errors.noHostname: Choose the address the VPN answers on first.
errors.noApiKey: The control server started but did not let Polaris in. Press Retry in a minute.
errors.notAllowed: Only an administrator can do that.
errors.notFound: That device is no longer on the VPN.
errors.badName: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 63 characters.
errors.badAuthId: This link is not a device request from this VPN.
errors.notApplied: The control server could not be started. Press Retry; if it keeps failing, open its service in Deploy.
errors.invalid: Something in the request was not valid. Reload the page and try again.
errors.generic: The VPN did not answer. Try again in a moment.
errors.limited: Private networks need the full edition: this one has no way to start a gateway.
errors.tooMany: This VPN already has as many networks as it can keep.
errors.subnetTaken: Another network already uses part of that subnet.
errors.noServer: That server is no longer available.
errors.gatewayFailed: The network was saved, but its server could not start the gateway. Press Retry when it is back.

zoneErrors.no-domain: There is no domain to put the VPN on yet. Add one in Domains.
zoneErrors.unknown-zone: That domain is not one you can use. Pick another.
zoneErrors.unverified: That domain is not verified yet. Finish it in Domains.
zoneErrors.bad-name: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

overview.title: Status
overview.keptHint: Its devices are kept. They sign back in by themselves when you turn it on.
overview.askAdmin: An administrator turns the VPN on. Your devices can be added once it runs.

stateHint.running: Devices can sign in and reach each other.
stateHint.failed: The control server could not be started.

turnOff.title: Turn the VPN off?
turnOff.body: Every device loses its connection until it is turned on again. The devices and their addresses are kept.

remove.title: Remove the VPN and all its devices
remove.body: Deletes the control server, its address and every device on it. Each device has to be added again afterwards.
remove.confirm: This deletes every device on the VPN for everybody, and cannot be undone.

hostname.label: Address
hostname.hint: Devices are pointed at this address. It stays until the VPN is removed.
hostname.taken: {hostname} is already in use. Pick another name.
hostname.invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
hostname.noZones: The VPN needs an address in one of your domains, and there is none yet.

devices.intro: Your devices on the VPN. Each reaches your other devices and the Polaris servers.
devices.adminIntro: Every device on the VPN. People reach only their own; administrators reach all of them.
devices.emptyBody: Install the Tailscale app on a device and point it at this VPN.
devices.removeBody: It is signed out of the VPN and has to be added again to come back.
devices.name: Name of the device
devices.badName: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 63 characters.

add.qrHint: Scan it on a phone to copy the address into the Tailscale app.
add.notRunning: The VPN is not on yet, so no device can be added.
add.keyTitle: A key for a server, router or TV
add.keyBody: For a device that cannot open a browser to sign in. The key adds one device to your account and stops working after an hour.

windows.name: Windows
windows.step1: Install Tailscale for Windows from tailscale.com/download.
windows.step2: Open this page in the Polaris app and press Join this network.

macos.name: macOS
macos.step1: Install Tailscale for macOS from the App Store or tailscale.com/download.
macos.step2: Open this page in the Polaris app and press Join this network.

linux.name: Linux
linux.step2: Open this page in the Polaris app and press Join this network.

ios.name: iPhone and iPad
ios.step1: Install Tailscale from the App Store and open it.
ios.step2: Tap the profile icon in the top-right corner, then Log in (or the account already signed in).
ios.step3: Open the menu in the top-right corner, choose Use a custom coordination server, enter this VPN's address and tap Log in.
ios.step4: Polaris opens. Press Add this device.

android.name: Android
android.step1: Install Tailscale from Google Play and open it.
android.step2: Tap the profile icon in the top-right corner, then Log in (or the account already signed in).
android.step3: Open the menu in the top-right corner, choose Use an alternate server, enter this VPN's address and tap Log in.
android.step4: Polaris opens. Press Add this device.

androidTv.name: Android TV
androidTv.step1: Install Tailscale from Google Play on the TV.
androidTv.step2: Open its menu, choose Use an alternate server and enter this VPN's address.
androidTv.step3: If the TV shows a code or link, open it on your phone and press Add this device there.

appleTv.name: Apple TV
appleTv.step1: Install Tailscale from the App Store on the Apple TV.
appleTv.step2: Open the Settings app, go to Apps, Tailscale, select URL under Alternate coordination server URL, enter this VPN's address and select Done.
appleTv.step3: Go back to Tailscale and sign in; open the link it shows on your phone and press Add this device.

router.name: Router or server
router.step1: Install Tailscale on it: most routers that run OpenWrt, pfSense or OPNsense offer it as a package.
router.step2: Create a key below and run the command with it on the device. It joins your devices with no browser.

add.noClient: Tailscale is not installed on this computer.
add.joinFailed: This computer could not join the network. Try again.

register.title: Add this device to the VPN?
register.body: A device asked to join. It is added to {account}'s devices and reaches only them. Add it only if you just signed it in yourself.
register.adminBody: A device asked to join. It is added to {account}'s devices and, because {account} is an administrator, reaches every device on the VPN. Add it only if you just signed it in yourself.
register.addedBody: The device is connected. You can close this page.
register.badBody: It is not a device request from this VPN. Start signing in again from the Tailscale app.

networks.intro: A subnet that stays the same whichever line or router you use. Reach it from anywhere through the VPN.
networks.memberIntro: Networks you can reach while connected to the VPN.
networks.emptyBody: Create one for your home devices. Its Wi-Fi and addresses stay the same when you change provider.
networks.memberEmptyBody: An administrator has not shared a network with you.
networks.createBody: Pick a server on the same network as the router. It carries this subnet into the VPN.
networks.name: Name
networks.subnetHint: Use 10.x.x.x or 192.168.x.x, between /16 and /29. Avoid 192.168.0.x and 192.168.1.x: providers' routers use them.
networks.badSubnet: Use a 10.x.x.x or 192.168.x.x subnet between /16 and /29.
networks.badRouter: It must be an address inside the subnet.
networks.subnetTaken: Another network already uses this subnet.
networks.ssidLong: Too long for a Wi-Fi name: accents and symbols count double.
networks.noServers: Add a server first: a gateway needs one to run on.
networks.internetHint: Leave off for local devices. Devices that depend on a vendor's cloud need it.
networks.editBody: Its subnet and server stay. Run the router setup again if you change internet access.
networks.removeBody: It stops being reachable through the VPN. Your router keeps its Wi-Fi until you remove it there.

stateHint.waiting: This takes under a minute. If it stays here, press Retry.
stateHint.offline: Check that {server} is on, then press Retry.
stateHint.unapproved: The route is approved the next time this page updates.

networks.routerMissingHint: {address} does not answer from {server}. Set up the router below, and make sure that server is connected to it.
networks.setupBody: Enter these values on any router. Keep them when you change router and nothing else needs changing.
networks.passwordLost: This password could not be read here. Remove the network and create it again.
networks.ruleLan: Allow the network {server} is on to reach {cidr}.
networks.ruleDevices: Block {cidr} from reaching your other networks.
networks.openWrtBody: Run this once on the router, and again on a replacement router.
networks.openWrtNoRadio: On a router with no Wi-Fi, add a free port to the bridge {bridge} and connect an access point there.
networks.linesBody: Connect each line to the router and let the router choose. On OpenWrt, use the mwan3 package. Polaris keeps reaching this network either way.

connect.empty: No devices yet. A device appears here the first time it connects.
connect.noNodes: No servers are available to you yet.
connect.torHint: Tor is free and more private, but much slower. Some sites block it, and calls or games will not work.

standing.none: You do not have VPN access. Ask an administrator for it.
standing.suspended: Your VPN access is suspended. Ask an administrator.
standing.expired: Your VPN access has expired. Ask an administrator.
standing.overLimit: You have used this month's traffic. It renews next month.

errors.noRoot: Polaris needs root on that machine. Edit its connection in Servers.
errors.unreachable: That machine did not answer. Check it is on and try again.
errors.unsupported: That machine's system is not supported. Use Debian or Ubuntu.
errors.noAccess: You do not have access to that server.
errors.deviceLimit: You have reached your device limit.
errors.nodeFull: That server is full. Pick another one.
errors.nodeNotReady: That server is still being set up. Try again in a minute.
errors.tooManyNodes: This Polaris has reached its limit of servers.
errors.invalid: Check the fields and try again.

connect.useApps: {clientKind, select, desktop {Connect from this app, or from the Polaris extension for just one browser.} other {Connect from the Polaris app on your computer, or from the Polaris extension for just this browser.}}
connect.noPhoneApp: There is no Polaris app for phones yet.

tunnel.denied: The VPN needs your permission once to install. Press Connect and accept the prompt.
tunnel.failed: This computer could not start the VPN. Try again.
tunnel.noAnswer: That server did not answer. Try another location.
tunnel.unreachable: That server's address could not be found. Try another location.

connect.remoteAccess: Tailscale and other ways into this server

own.title: Your own VPNs
own.hint: Import a WireGuard file from a provider such as Proton or Mullvad. It connects from the Polaris app on your computer.
own.added: {count, plural, one {# VPN added} other {# VPNs added}}
own.rejected: Not WireGuard files with one server: {names}
own.removeBody: Its file is deleted from Polaris. You would need to import it again to connect.

errors.tooMany: You can keep up to {limit} VPNs. Remove some first.
errors.unreadable: Those files could not be read. Use the .conf files your provider gives you.

nodes.title: Servers
nodes.hint: Machines people connect through. Add as many as you like.
nodes.addBody: Polaris sets it up over the connection it already has.
nodes.notYours: Only the administrator who owns this machine can change it.
nodes.leftRunning: The VPN on this server could not be removed, so it keeps running there.
nodes.editBody: Devices keep working. A new address or port needs each device added again.
nodes.empty: No servers yet. People cannot connect until you add one.
nodes.noMachines: Every machine with root is already a server. Add another in Servers.
nodes.name: Name
nodes.torHint: Free and more private, but much slower. Only web-style traffic passes.
nodes.portHint: UDP {port} has to be open towards this machine.
nodes.privateEndpoint: That is a private address. Use a public one, or devices outside can't connect, and forward UDP {port} on your router.
nodes.removeBody: Its devices stop working and are removed.
nodes.unreachableBody: That machine did not answer, so it may keep running the VPN and letting its devices in until it is reinstalled.

people.title: People
people.hint: Who may connect, through which servers, and how much.
people.addBody: They need an account on this Polaris.
people.editBody: Changes reach the servers right away.
people.openHint: Anyone with an account may connect, with {count} devices. Limits below still apply to the people listed.
people.empty: Nobody has been given access yet. Administrators can always connect.

mesh.title: Private networks
mesh.hint: Optional: lets devices reach each other and a home network. Normal VPN use does not need it.
